name: gh-resolve
description: Recover a blocked GitHub PR: red CI, rebase conflicts, or an out-of-date base.
skillInstructions:
Kimi Code tool mapping for the gh-resolve skills.

The authoritative mapping is not in this repo. It lives in the sibling repo `dEitY719/harness-skills` at `references/kimi-tools.md` (https://github.com/dEitY719/harness-skills/blob/main/references/kimi-tools.md) and is the single source of truth for every repo in the `dEitY719/*-skills` family; do not copy it here. Summary:

- "Ask the user" -> `AskUserQuestion`. `gh-resolve:conflict` resolves each conflicting hunk against the user's intent: an ambiguous conflict must be asked about, never guessed. Kimi has the tool, so use it.
- `TodoWrite` -> Kimi Code's `TodoList` tool.
- "Dispatch a subagent" -> `Agent` with `subagent_type: "coder"` (implementation) or `"explore"` (read-only). Never pass `general-purpose`.
- Read / Write / Edit / Bash / Grep / Glob keep their exposed Kimi names. Every `git` and `gh` call in these skills is a plain shell command - run it with `Bash` and surface its `[OK]` / `[WARN]` / `[FAIL]` lines verbatim.
- `gh` must be installed and authenticated. Each skill binds `TARGET_HOST` and `TARGET_REPO` from the remote URL and prefixes every call with `GH_HOST=` before any API call (#1403). Do not drop that prefix; a GHES remote resolves to the wrong server without it.
- Kimi Code has no `Skill` tool. Where `gh-resolve:outdated` delegates to `gh-resolve:conflict` on a `CONFLICTING` PR, exit with the documented code and tell the user which skill to run; do not silently inline the other skill's rebase loop.

Safety contracts. These are part of the skills, not advice:

- `gh-resolve:conflict` and `gh-resolve:outdated` push with `--force-with-lease`. Never substitute plain `--force`. A rejected lease means someone else pushed: stop, surface the divergence, and let the user decide - never re-fetch and re-rebase on their behalf.
- Neither rebase skill runs on the repo's default branch, and neither creates or removes a `--worktree` path; the caller owns that lifecycle.
- `gh-resolve:conflict` never auto-resolves an ambiguous conflict and never introduces a merge commit.
- `gh-resolve:ci-fail` fast-forward pushes only - no force of any kind - and refuses to push while the local lint/test run is still red (CI infinite-loop guard). It removes the `CI fail` label only after the push succeeds, and never blind-retries a failing job.
- All three print `BACKUP_SHA` before touching history so the user can `git reset --hard <sha>`.
- None of them adds `review-passed` or `review-blocked`, and none removes `review-blocked`. Removing a stale `review-passed` after a successful force-push is mandatory (#1563).

interface.shortDescription: Unblock a stuck GitHub pull request
interface.longDescription: gh-resolve bundles the three PR blocked-state recovery skills: ci-fail, conflict, and outdated.
